sources.title: Xiong Rui, Borel-Weil and Borel-Weil-Bott, Lecture 1 (course notes)
sources.locator: Lecture 1 (Borel-Weil Theorem), Sections 1.5-1.8, 1.9, 1.12-1.20 and 1.22, printed pp. 2-7, read in full over that range: characters and associated line bundles (1.5-1.6), tautological bundles (1.7), Borel-Weil via the G-bimodule decomposition of C[G] (1.8), canonical bundle and Serre duality (1.9), Pluecker embedding (1.12-1.13), rank-one fibres and the P1 table (1.14-1.15), the Borel-Weil-Bott shift and its n=-1, n=0, general cases (1.16-1.19), the principal block (1.20) and the Atiyah-Bott/Weyl-character check (1.22)

contents.name: 1.5-1.6 characters of T, the one-dimensional module C(lambda), the associated bundle xi(lambda)=G x^B C(lambda) with section sheaf O(lambda), and the fact that every equivariant line bundle arises this way
contents.note: Sign translation: Rui writes the fibre module C(lambda) with T acting by lambda^{-1}, which is exactly the library's C_{-lambda}; his statement that O(x_1)=O(1) on the flag variety of SL2 matches the published sl2 example.

contents.name: 1.7 tautological bundles phi_k on the type-A flag variety and phi_k/phi_{k-1}=O(-x_k); for n=2, O(x_1)=O(1)
contents.proof_mapping: the rank-one identification O(x_1)=O(1) is the SL2 case of the line-bundle identification proved in the published ex-sl2-flag-variety-line-bundles and used by the example

contents.name: 1.8 Borel-Weil theorem: H^0(G/B,O(lambda))^* = L(lambda) for dominant lambda and 0 otherwise, proved from the G-bimodule decomposition C[G]=bigoplus L(lambda)^* otimes L(lambda)
1.9 tangent bundle computation gr Omega^1 = bigoplus O(-alpha_i), canonical bundle omega = O(-2rho), and Serre duality H^{N-i}(O(-2rho-lambda)) = H^i(O(lambda))^*
contents.note: The canonical-bundle half is the published AG item; the Serre pairing half is inlined in prop-borel-weil-bott-is-compatible-with-serre-duality, which records the same N-i pairing.

contents.name: 1.10-1.11 standard parabolics P_J, partial flag varieties, and the type-A descriptions including n=k+(n-k) Grassmannians
contents.reason: The pair consumes only the minimal parabolic P_i and its projective-line fibres, which are supplied by the published AG items; the general P_J and type-A partial-flag combinatorics are not used by any item of this pair and building them would duplicate AG ownership.

contents.name: 1.12-1.13 Pluecker embedding by L(rho) (and by L(lambda) for general lambda) and the Grassmannian identification
contents.note: The published AG orbit-quotient item constructs X=G/B as the closed orbit in P(L(2rho)) and the Pluecker-rational modules; the general-lambda Pluecker statement is not needed beyond that construction.

contents.name: 1.14 rank-one subgroup SL2 -> P_i, the isomorphism P1 = P_i/B, restriction degree <alpha_i^vee,lambda> of O(lambda), and the P/B fibre-bundle structure of G/B -> G/P
contents.note: The degree computation is the published AG item; the fibre-bundle structure and the rank-one subgroup are thm-minimal-parabolic-flag-projection-is-p1-bundle and lem-semisimple-rank-one-sl2-root-homomorphism.

contents.name: 1.15 the table of H^0 and H^1 of O(n) on P1 for all n, including the vanishing at n=-1, and the Serre pairing on P1
1.16-1.19 Borel-Weil-Bott shift H^i(G/B,O(lambda)) = H^{i+1}(G/B,O(s_i dot lambda)) for <alpha_i^vee,lambda> >= -1, with the n=-1, n=0, and general-filtration proofs
contents.proof_mapping: the adopted manifest proof uses the published relative P1 shift theorem together with the relative canonical identification, in place of Rui's p^*p_* filtration; the resulting degree-one shift is the same statement

contents.name: 1.20 principal block: dim H^i(G/B,O(w dot 0)) = 1 for i=l(w) and 0 otherwise
contents.proof_mapping: specialisation of the BWB degree count at the weight lambda = w dot 0, where w dot lambda = 0 and L(0) is one-dimensional; the general theorem contains this row

contents.name: 1.21-1.22 Atiyah-Bott localisation computation of the Euler character and the derivation of the Weyl character formula
contents.reason: The localisation theorem for torus actions is not part of this library's development and the pair's Euler-character corollary is instead obtained from Borel-Weil-Bott together with the published Weyl character formula of the RL-7 page; the source's check is recorded as an independent treatment, not scaffolded.

contents.name: 1.23 Weyl character formula as a Schur polynomial for GL_n
contents.reason: The GL_n symmetric-function specialisation belongs to the Littlewood-Richardson and Schur-module development (the paired page tensor-product-multiplicities-and-littlewood-richardson); it is not consumed by any Borel-Weil-Bott item here.

sources.title: Joshua Ng (Hoi Hei Jan Sum), The Borel-Weil-Bott Theorem (Chicago REU 2015)
sources.locator: Sections 3-6, printed pp. 6-14, read in full: vector and line bundles (Section 3), homogeneous bundles and local triviality (3.5-3.7), Bruhat decomposition (3.9) and the SL2 example (3.10), induced and restricted representations (4.1-4.4), Schur's lemma (4.5), the Borel-Weil theorem and its proof (5.1-5.4) with the SL2 computation (5.5), and the Pluecker embedding (6.1-6.3)

contents.name: Section 3 Definitions 3.1-3.2 of vector and line bundles and Examples 3.3-3.4 (trivial and tautological bundles)
contents.proof_mapping: the section identification works with the bundle and gluing formalism of these definitions, using the published AG torsor charts for the local triviality

contents.name: Theorem 3.6 the homogeneous bundle G x^H V -> G/H is a vector bundle and Proposition 3.7 local triviality of G -> G/B via the Bruhat decomposition
Section 4 Definitions 4.1-4.3 global sections, the induced representation Ind_B^G V and restriction, and Remark 4.4
contents.proof_mapping: the induced-module structure on global sections and its G-action are exactly the proposition; the restriction functor is the passing of the G-action to B used by the reciprocity and character computations

contents.name: Lemma 4.5 Schur's lemma for finite-dimensional irreducible representations
contents.reason: The adopted proof of the Borel-Weil theorem counts constituents through complete reducibility and the one-dimensional nilradical-invariant lines, so Schur's lemma is not a proof dependency of any item of this pair; the source uses it only in its alternative multiplicity computation.

contents.name: Theorem 5.1 Lie-Kolchin and Theorem 5.2 classification of irreducible finite-dimensional representations of connected solvable groups
contents.reason: The adopted Borel-Weil route replaces the solvable-group representation classification by the unipotent-radical invariants of finite-dimensional g-modules; neither theorem is consumed, and the compact/solvable representation theory is owned by other pages.

contents.name: Theorem 5.3 the Borel-Weil theorem: Ind_B^G W is the dual of the irreducible of highest weight -chi when -chi is dominant integral, and 0 otherwise
Lemma 5.4 Frobenius reciprocity Hom_G(V, Ind_B^G W) = Hom_B(V,W)
contents.proof_mapping: Ng's evaluation-at-the-base-point reciprocity is the independent treatment of the H^0 computation; the manifest route instead uses the big-cell uniqueness of nilradical-invariant sections together with complete reducibility, so the reciprocity statement is recorded as source background and a check, not as a dependency

contents.name: Example 5.5 computation of all line bundles on P1 for SL2 and their global sections as homogeneous polynomials
Theorem 6.1 Pluecker embedding by a dominant regular weight, Theorem 6.2 the product-of-fundamentals embedding, Theorem 6.3 i^*L = G x^B C_lambda
Example 3.10 the SL_n flag variety as the variety of complete flags
contents.reason: The pair works with the abstract flag variety G/B supplied by the published AG items; the type-A flag identification is not consumed by any Borel-Weil-Bott item, and the SL2 and SL3 instances are covered by the published examples cited in the B companion.

contents.name: Theorem 1: for semisimple simply connected G the forgetful functor from equivariant line bundles on G/B to line bundles is an equivalence
contents.note: The published AG classification covers the equivariant line bundles by characters of B; the essential-surjectivity half (every line bundle is equivariant) is the additional content of Lurie's Theorem 1 and is not consumed by any item of this pair.

contents.name: Theorem 2: H^0(X,L_lambda)=0 unless -lambda is dominant, and if -lambda is dominant it is irreducible of lowest weight lambda, dual to the highest weight -lambda representation
Proof of Theorem 2: identification with functions satisfying the functional equation, U'-invariants at most one-dimensional, and the SL2/pole-extension construction for the nonzero vector
contents.proof_mapping: the big-cell function, the codimension-one Bruhat cells and the SL2 computation a^k are exactly the strategy of the extension lemma; the uniqueness half is lem-a-nonzero-dominant-section-is-determined-on-the-big-cell

contents.name: Theorem 3: for a P1-bundle with fibre degree n >= -1, H^i(E,L) = H^{i+1}(E, L otimes K^{n+1})
Lemma 4: H^i(X,L_lambda) = H^{i+1}(X,L_{w_alpha(lambda)}) for <alpha^vee,lambda> >= 0
contents.proof_mapping: the manifest lemma restates the shift in the library's indexing with the relative canonical bundle L_{-alpha}; the two formulations agree after lambda -> lambda-rho

contents.name: Singular case: a wall-stabilised weight gives H^i = H^{i+1} for all i and all cohomology vanishes
Theorem 5: Borel-Weil-Bott, regular case with the unique nonvanishing degree l(w) and dual of the irreducible of highest weight w(lambda)-rho
Final Serre-duality step in the proof of Theorem 5: H^i(X,L_lambda) dual to H^{n-i}(X,L_{-lambda}) via the canonical bundle L_{2rho}

sources.title: George Boxer and Vincent Pilloni, Notes on Higher Coleman Theory (Montreal lectures, December 2020)
sources.locator: Lecture 1, Sections 1.1.1-1.1.6, printed pp. 2-6, read in full: line bundle conventions and the dotted action (1.1.1), Borel-Weil-Bott Theorem 1.1 (1.1.2), the Cousin complex and its properties (1.1.3), the P1 example (1.1.4), the big-weight amplitude Proposition 1.5 (1.1.5) and interpolation (1.1.6)

contents.name: 1.1.1 conventions: Bruhat stratification, dotted action w dot kappa = w(kappa+rho)-rho, and the line bundle L_kappa with sections f(bu)=w_0 kappa(b) f(u)
contents.note: Convention translation: with kappa = -w_0 lambda the section equation becomes f(gb)=lambda(b)f(g), so BP's L_kappa is the library's L_{w_0 kappa} = G x^B C_{-w_0 kappa}; this is the sign translation recorded in the design and in the batch notes, not a mathematical conflict.

contents.name: Theorem 1.1 Borel-Weil-Bott: either no w makes w dot kappa dominant and all cohomology vanishes, or a unique such w exists and RGamma(FL,L_kappa) = H^{l(w)}[-l(w)] with H^{l(w)} the highest weight w dot kappa representation
Remark 1.2: the vanishing alternative happens exactly when kappa+rho is not G-regular
1.1.3 the Grothendieck-Cousin complex, its quasi-isomorphism to RGamma(FL,L_kappa), and the affine-space local-cohomology computation on which the proof rests
contents.reason: The Cousin-complex/local-cohomology proof route requires local cohomology with support, Cousin complexes and their g-equivariance, none of which exist in this library; the pair instead adopts the rank-one P1-induction proof, and BP remains the independent treatment of the statement.

contents.name: 1.1.4 the explicit P1 Cousin complex computation and the weight ranges k, k-2, ... and -k-2, ...
contents.proof_mapping: the displayed weight ranges are the SL2 line-bundle table verified by the example through the published O(d) cohomology item

contents.name: Lemma 1.4 and Proposition 1.5: the weights of local cohomology are bounded by w^{-1}w_0 dot kappa, and the big-weight part has amplitude [min d-l(w), max d-l(w)]
contents.proof_mapping: this is an independent proof of the unique surviving cohomological degree in the regular case, equivalently the degree count l(w) of the manifest theorem; it is recorded as a source check rather than as a dependency

contents.name: 1.1.6 interpolation of the sheaves L_kappa and of the local cohomology in the parameter
contents.reason: The interpolation statement is a p-adic/formal-family construction of higher Coleman theory, not part of the complex Borel-Weil-Bott theorem consumed here; it needs completed group rings and formal schemes not present in this pair.
